_note: P7.4 What's this? help: one or two short lines per money or deal word. Keys are concept ids in Data/ui/lexicon.json; the word shown is the lexicon word for the active mode. Lines follow Docs/word-bible.md.

maxChars.source: Docs/word-bible.md readable by a 12 year old

company_cash: Money the company has right now.
Building, staff and loan payments come out of it.
personal_cash: Your own money, kept apart from the company.
pay_yourself: Move money from the company to you.
The company has less to build with after.
cash_put_in: The money you paid from your own pocket for a project, not borrowed.
cash_to_you: What you keep from a sale after loans, fees and tax are paid.
yearly_income: Rent in a year, minus the cost to run the buildings.
Loan payments are not taken out yet.
quarter_income: Rent this quarter, minus the cost to run the buildings.
rent: What tenants pay you to use your space.
value: What a buyer would likely pay for it today.
land_value: What the empty ground is worth without buildings.
holding_cost: What it costs each quarter just to own it: tax, upkeep and loan payments.
project_verdict: Compares what a project earns with what it cost.
Pays for itself is good. Loses money means rent is too low for the cost.
payroll: What you pay your staff each quarter.
lender: A bank or fund that lends you money for a project.
lender_type: The kind of lender. Each one lends a different amount at a different price.
loan_payment: What you pay the lender each month, interest and some of the loan.
capital_stack: How a project is paid for: your cash, loans and partner money.
risk_presets: Safe borrows less. Risky borrows more, so profits and losses both get bigger.
layer_senior: The biggest loan. It gets paid back before anyone else.
layer_mezz: A smaller loan on top of the main one. It costs more because it is paid back second.
layer_pref: Partner money that gets its return before you see a profit.
layer_investor: Money from investors who share in the profit with you.
ltv: How much you owe compared with what the building is worth.
dscr: How many times your income covers your loan payments. Under 1 means you cannot pay.
income_drop_to_default: How far income can fall before you cannot make the loan payment.
cap_rate: Yearly income divided by price. Buyers pay more when it is low.
interest_rate: The full yearly price of the loan, base rate plus the lender's extra.
base_rate: The rate every loan in town starts from. It moves with the market.
loan_spread: What the lender adds on top of the base rate.
dev_spread: What a project earns over what buyers expect. Bigger is safer.
floating_rate: Your loan payment moves up or down when rates change.
fixed_rate: Your loan payment stays the same until the loan ends.
missed_payment: You did not pay the lender on time. Miss too many and you can lose the building.
foreclosure: The lender takes the building because the loan was not paid.
credit_line: A backup loan that covers you when cash runs out. It charges interest.
refinance: Swap your loan for a new one, often to pull cash out of a finished building.
investor_target: The return investors get before you share in the profit.
promote: Your extra share of the profit once investors get their target.
backs_out: Someone walks away from a deal after saying yes.
check_size: How much money an investor puts in.
offer: The price you say you will pay or take.
counter_offer: A new price sent back after an offer.
handshake_deal: A promise with no contract. Breaking it hurts your honor.
diligence: Check the land before you buy: who owns it, the ground and the rules.
title_problem: Someone else may have a claim on the land. Fix it before you build.
dirty_ground: The soil needs cleaning before anyone can build. That costs money and time.
easement: Someone else has a right to cross part of the land.
off_market: A deal no other buyer has seen, so you can pay less.
distressed: An owner who has to sell soon, often for less.
auction: Land sold at the courthouse to the highest bid. You pay fast.
infill: An empty lot inside town, close to people and roads.
sell: Sell a property to a buyer. Loans get paid off from the price.
closing: The day a sale is done and the money moves.
roll_over: Put sale profit into a new deal before a deadline to put off the tax.
exit_tax: Tax on the profit when you sell.
buyer_reit: A big company that buys many buildings. It pays well for steady rent.
buyer_private: A local investor. Faster, but often pays less.
buyer_1031: A buyer who must buy before a deadline, so may pay a little more.
go_public: Sell shares of your company to the public for a lot of cash.
shareholders: People who own part of your company and want income each quarter.
quarter_target: The income you promised shareholders. Missing it drops your share price.
seller_note: You lend the buyer part of the price and they pay you back over time.
heat: How much the city is watching you. Five stars starts an investigation.
honor: How fair people think you are. High honor opens doors.
bad_sport: A tag for backing out of deals. New deals freeze while you have it.
